clue.text: Start to shake with mirth that's killing

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of shake is wanted

parts.note: mirth is laughter, merriment

explanation.surface: Someone shakes with helpless laughter at a joke that is killing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killing' reads as 'hilarious', tied to the mirth, but it defines the noun: a slaughter is a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughter is a large-scale or brutal killing, so the nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: A model may be drawn to it, but not an overweight one

definitions.text: A model may be drawn to it, but not an overweight one

parts.words: A model may be drawn to it, but not an overweight one
parts.note: a model is drawn in proportion to a ratio, while an overweight person shies away from the bathroom weighing device

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses in one: a scale model is drawn to a fixed ratio, and the weighing scales are what an overweight person avoids; 'model' also suggests a catwalk model.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a ratio used in drawing and a weighing machine, covering both halves.

clue.text: Athlete out of place on the track

definitions.text: Athlete out of place on the track

parts.words: Athlete out of place on the track
parts.note: a runner who finished outside the first three places, unplaced in a race

explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' suggests someone who does not belong there; it means not finishing in a placing.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a competitor who fails to finish among the placed runners in a race.

clue.text: Obtain promotion to board

definitions.meaning: to advance or succeed in one's career
to climb aboard a bus, train or other vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to make progress in a career and to climb aboard transport.

clue.text: Store up trouble for travelling performers

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up and disturb it, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone is warned that hoarding things will lead to difficulties later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' looks like the object of 'Store up'; it is the anagram signal working on STOREUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Troupes are companies of actors or entertainers, often touring from place to place.

clue.text: Copy special procedure

indicators.note: a special version is made out of the ordinary, signalling that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An office instruction about the particular way documents must be duplicated.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproduce something is to make a copy of it.

clue.text: Novel companion for Nelson

definitions.meaning: a Jane Austen novel named after its matchmaking heroine
Lady Hamilton, by first name, was the mistress of Admiral Horatio Nelson

explanation.walkthrough: Nelson is Admiral Lord Nelson, Britain's naval hero, whose famous lover was Lady Hamilton.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both the title of an Austen book and the first name of Nelson's mistress.

clue.text: Professors discharged, ie elevated and retaining worth

indicators.note: the reversed pair holds the other piece within it
in a down clue, lifting the letters reads them from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
merit is worth or value

explanation.surface: Retired academics are said to be promoted and to keep their value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns IE into EI, which then holds MERIT: E(MERIT)I.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeriti are professors who have retired, keeping their title as an honour.

clue.text: Model male, born one of five

parts.note: a man is a male
NE, from French née, marks a maiden name: born
a quin is one of quintuplets

explanation.surface: A male model's biography: born as one of quintuplets.
explanation.definitionFit: A mannequin is a dummy used to display clothes, or a fashion model.

clue.text: Raised voice in row on river

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it follows it

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a set-to is a quarrel or row

explanation.surface: A heated argument breaks out on a riverbank and voices are raised.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, south-west England. 'Raised voice' suggests shouting but means a high singing register.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a male singing voice pitched above the normal range.

clue.text: Songs of Praise?

parts.note: read literally, songs that praise or exalt, rather than the TV programme

explanation.walkthrough: Songs of Praise is a long-running BBC Sunday hymn programme; the question mark tells you to read the title literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Paeans are songs or hymns of praise or triumph.

clue.text: Chicken quarters?

parts.note: not cuts of a bird but the enclosed place where poultry live

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken quarters' suggests jointed portions of chicken; quarters here means living accommodation.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen run is an enclosure where chickens are kept.

clue.text: Brief biographies of professional record holders

parts.note: pro is short for professional
files hold records

explanation.surface: Short life stories written about sports champions who hold records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record holders' suggests champions; it means the folders that hold records.
explanation.definitionFit: Profiles are short descriptive accounts of a person's life and character.

clue.text: Start firing to make things lively

definitions.meaning: to liven up or get going

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to begin shooting and to become animated or expansive.

clue.text: Vessel — right one in which to serve stew

parts.note: a pot is a vessel
to pour is to serve a drink
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction to use the proper pot for serving a stew.
explanation.definitionFit: Potpourri originally meant a stew of mixed meats, from the Spanish olla podrida.

clue.text: Opt for oil production as responsibility of minister

indicators.note: the letters are produced in a new form, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Choosing oil production as the job of a government minister for energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' looks like part of the phrase 'oil production'; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister's portfolio is the department or area of government they are responsible for.

clue.text: Academic bosses must admit financial liability

indicators.note: admitting someone lets them in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: studs are bosses, raised knobs on a surface
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: University bosses are forced to own up to a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bosses' suggests managers; it means studs, ornamental knobs.
explanation.definitionFit: A studious person is devoted to study, academic in temperament.

clue.text: Sci-fi shows celebrity to take long, hard journey

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
a trek is a long arduous journey

explanation.surface: A famous actor sets off on a gruelling expedition in a science-fiction series.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Trek is a long-running franchise of science-fiction television series and films.

clue.text: Put up alternative English academic for girl's school

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word up reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
a dean is a senior academic

explanation.surface: An alternative English academic is nominated for a post at a girls' school.
explanation.walkthrough: Roedean is a well-known girls' boarding school near Brighton in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Roedean is a famous independent boarding school for girls in Sussex.

clue.text: There's pleasure after the game but he spoils it

indicators.note: one piece placed after the other in the answer

parts.note: in hunting, the kill is the game that has been brought down
joy is pleasure

explanation.surface: Someone ruins the fun after a match that everyone enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the game' suggests a sporting match; in hunting the kill is the game slain.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy is someone who spoils other people's enjoyment.

clue.text: In conclusion, it's the ultimate gin cocktail

parts.note: the ultimate is the end, the final point

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A drinker declares one gin cocktail to be the best of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' mixes GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is a conclusion, the final part of something.

clue.text: Raising hat to a girl presents a problem

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word reads it upwards, backwards

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man unsure whether to doff his hat to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' turns LID into DIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a problem involving a difficult choice.

clue.text: Strong, pure flow in circulation

indicators.note: circulating moves things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a strong, clean stream of water flowing round a system.
explanation.definitionFit: Powerful means having great strength or force.

clue.text: Mum, listen for a change!

indicators.note: changing the word alters the order of its letters

explanation.surface: An exasperated plea for Mother to pay attention for once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like Mother; it means quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum as an adjective means silent, saying nothing.

clue.text: Football kit angrily torn off

definitions.meaning: the shirt, shorts and socks a team wears
as in the idiom 'tear a ... off', to rebuke angrily, and to ... as to tear away

explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a football team's kit is its strip; to tear a strip off someone is to scold them furiously.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a team's uniform and also means to tear away a covering.

clue.text: Approaches a listener in different ways

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: N and S, north and south, are two opposite compass directions
an ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone approaches a listener from various directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different ways' gives two compass points, N and S, around EAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Nears means comes close to, approaches.

clue.text: Test of French in viva voce

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a viva voce is an oral examination
de is French for of

explanation.surface: An oral examination in the French language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test of French' reads as a language exam; 'of French' means the French word for 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a severe test of endurance, and historically a trial of guilt.

clue.text: One in jam here sadly, a doleful character

indicators.note: the single letter is placed among the other letters
sadly signals that the letters are treated badly, disordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gloomy person stuck in a tight spot laments their situation.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes into JAMHERE and the lot is rearranged. Jeremiah, the Old Testament prophet of doom, gives his name to a habitual pessimist.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jeremiah is a person who constantly complains or prophesies disaster.

clue.text: Main shareholder?

parts.note: the beast that takes the largest portion, from the idiom for the biggest part, also a creature with a mane

explanation.walkthrough: 'shareholder' suggests investors; it alludes to the lion's share, the biggest portion, and 'Main' puns on the mane.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'the lion's share' makes this animal the one holding the main share.

clue.text: Games periods

definitions.meaning: the modern Olympic Games, each celebration of which is one
a period of four years between successive Olympic Games in ancient Greece

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both celebrations of the Olympic Games and the four-year intervals between them.
